canonical_form.matching: case-insensitive; '-', '_' and ' ' are removed before matching
canonical_form.note: A manifest may spell a capability 'Filesystem', 'file-system' or 'file_system'. Normalisation maps all of them onto the canonical name, and an unrecognised spelling normalises to itself and is then refused as unknown.

default_deny: A capability name absent from this file is refused. It is never treated as pure, never ignored, and never assumed to be a subset of anything.

capabilities.name: core
capabilities.description: Baseline language execution. Also the requirement an unknown operation is refused under, so a manifest typo cannot widen access.

capabilities.name: clock
capabilities.description: Read the wall clock and sleep.

capabilities.name: environment
capabilities.description: Read and change the process working directory.

capabilities.name: filesystem
capabilities.description: Read, write, list, create and delete files. A whole-resource grant: there is no read/write split.

capabilities.name: process
capabilities.description: Spawn processes and terminate the program.

capabilities.name: network
capabilities.description: Outbound and inbound network connections, including HTTP.

capabilities.name: clipboard
capabilities.description: Read and write the system clipboard.

capabilities.name: device
capabilities.description: General device information such as battery level and model.

recognised_unlisted.name: gpu
recognised_unlisted.reason: Normalised and accepted by the manifest vocabulary, but no builtin in the requirement table declares it. A grant is recorded; nothing currently consults it.

recognised_unlisted.reason: As gpu: recognised, not currently required by any operation.

aliases.reason: pkg/capability spells location 'GPS'; the canonical name is lowercase and resource-independent.

planned.name: filesystem.read
planned.reason: Fine-grained sub-capabilities are documented as a planned refinement. The requirement table grants whole resources, so a program requesting 'filesystem' receives read and write together. Do not validate against these names: normalising 'filesystem.read' yields itself, which is absent from this file and is therefore refused.

enforcement.language_gate: compiler/compiler emits OpNativeCall for a direct, statically named call to a gated operation; the VM consults the grant before dispatch.
known_limitations: The `requires` clause and compile-time diagnostic E0201 do not exist in the grammar or the type checker. Refusal happens at run time, on the first gated call.
Indirect calls are not gated: `let f = writeFile; f("a", "b")` is not recognised at emission time.
The evaluator path uses a pre-scan that sees direct calls only. The VM path is the enforced one.
Pure-context effect checking is inert; the checker's pure-context flag is never enabled.
enforcement.os_gate: OnuronOS maps a declared capability onto real SELinux, service, file and device permissions. That mapping is the only complete boundary today; see docs/adr/0004.
